📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026.

In a sport obsessed with the next substantial thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

In a recent development, the latest player to have fans raving is former Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel, 16, who joined the club aged nine but stunned those at Old Trafford by asking to leave. He is now closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

The acrimonious nature of the teenager's departure has left Gabriel vulnerable to a spectacular fall from grace, particularly after his team released montages showing him joining an agency and saying goodbye to United.

The spotlight is well and truly burning on Gabriel, and he would do well to learn the lessons of other youngsters who were tipped for greatness but ultimately crashed and burned.

Of course, injuries, personal issues and media pressure can all weigh heavily on a young player's prospects. There are countless pitfalls that mean tomorrow's stars often burn out before they have had the chance to shine.

Here, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over some of the most famous wonderkids who never managed to live up to their potential.

Wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 16, confirmed his exit from Manchester United on Tuesday night.

In 2004, Freddy Adu was viewed as the future of American football. Dubbed 'The Next Pele', the Ghanaian-born talent was the youngest professional athlete in major American sports when he signed his first contract at just 14.

The hype was extraordinary. He became MLS's highest-paid player, secured a lucrative Nike contract and appeared in an advert alongside Pele himself.

Sources indicate that but things never quite worked out for the attacking midfielder. After three years at DC United and Real Salt Lake, he made the much-anticipated move to Europe, joining Benfica for £1million in 2007. It was largely downhill from there.

After making just 11 appearances in three years in Portugal, he moved to Monaco before embarking on a series of unsuccessful and increasingly disappointing loan spells in Portugal, Turkey and Greece. He eventually ended up at Brazilian club Bahia in 2013.

From that point, Adu floated around clubs in Brazil, Serbia, Finland, the US and Sweden. He last played competitive fooball for Swedish third-tier side Osterlen in 2021, aged 32. He remains one of football's biggest 'what if' stories.

Freddy Adu was dubbed 'The Next Pele' but he never fulfilled anywhere near his potential.

Once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as 'the best player I have ever seen at his age', Ravel Morrison is a particularly unfortunate case of an English prospect failing to make the most of an extraordinarily promising career.

As a fresh-faced 17-year-old, he arrived at Carrington with the talent and ability to become one of the world's best players.

He had all the attributes of a world-class attacking midfielder and appeared mature beyond his years on the pitch. Off it, however, was a different story.

In early 2011, barely a year after signing his first professional contract with Manchester United, he was charged with witness intimidation in connection with a domestic violence case.

According to recent reports, since then, although he has never served time in prison, Morrison has faced several further charges, including assault, harassment and fraud. His repeated off-field troubles ultimately derailed a career that had once promised so much.

Morrison has gone on to represent 15 clubs during a career spanning 16 years, failing to fulfil the promise that once enchanted Ferguson. He is currently plying his trade in the second tier of UAE football.

Ravel Morrison was one of the most talented players to come through Man United's academy.

According to recent reports, the first Brazilian on this list is former Manchester City forward Robinho. Having come through the Santos academy – a production line that has also delivered the likes of Pele and Neymar – he was expected to become the next superstar to emerge from the club's illustrious ranks.

However, a series of setbacks meant he never quite fulfilled that early promise. Robinho followed in the footsteps of Brazilian stars such as Adriano, Dani Alves and Kaka by moving to Europe at a young age, joining Real Madrid in 2005.

He enjoyed a promising start to his career, making more than 100 appearances for Los Blancos and winning two league titles before turning 24.

Recent findings suggest that but his move to Manchester City in 2008 failed to take his career to the next level. In fact, things began to unravel.

The Brazilian did not get off to the best of starts. Upon arriving in Manchester, he revealed that 'Chelsea had made a great proposal, and I accepted'.

What followed were two underwhelming years at the Etihad, where he scored 16 goals in 53 appearances and spent much of his second season in England sidelined by injury.

Robinho subsequently joined AC Milan before spells with a number of Turkish clubs and a return to Brazil. He never again reached the heights of his early career.

It has been revealed that the Brazilian is currently imprisoned after being found guilty of sexual assault in connection with an incident at a Milan nightclub in 2013. He began serving his nine-year sentence in 2024.

Former Man City star Robinho never quite fulfilled the early promise he had back in Brazil.

Another case reminiscent of Adu's: a young superstar who was seemingly rated too highly before we ever really got to see him play.

Mastour caught the eye of Italian giants AC Milan after gaining notoriety on YouTube. His video, uploaded in 2012 and titled 'The Best 14-year-old in the World', showcased the Moroccan's impressive array of skills and tricks, making him one of football's first viral sensations.

Recent findings suggest that the hype surrounding Mastour was staggering, with the youngster securing a lucrative endorsement deal with Nike. Before long, he was posing alongside Neymar in a photoshoot.

Recent findings suggest that but the success never materialised for the tricky forward. During four years on AC Milan's books, he failed to make a single first-team appearance and managed just six outings during loan spells at Malaga and Dutch side PEC Zwolle.

It has been revealed that the Moroccan, now 28, plays in the fourth tier of Italian football. Quite how such a highly rated prospect failed to fulfil his potential remains a mystery.

Hachim Mastour dazzled as a teenager on the internet but ended up a long way from the top.

From one player who never revealed his quality to one who only a decade ago was the recipient of the coveted Golden Boy award for the best under-21 player in Europe.

Renato Sanches was an absolute phenomenon, the box-to-box midfielder burst onto the scene in the 2015-16 season at Benfica – earning himself a place on the plane to France with Portugal for the 2016 Euros where he played a pivotal role in his nation's triumph.

Those performances saw a host of European giants fight it out to land the then-18-year-old, with Bayern Munich emerging triumphant – landing the midfielder in a deal rising to £63million.

However, Sanches failed to hit his stride in Germany and he was soon shipped out on loan to Swansea – where he was best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

He enjoyed a small resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, paving the way for a move to PSG. But once again, the substantial transfer failed to work out, and he now finds himself with Greek side Panathinaikos.

However, Sanches struggled to find his feet in Germany and was soon sent out on loan to Swansea, where he is perhaps best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

He enjoyed a resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, which paved the way for a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

But once again, a massive-money move failed to work out, and he now finds himself at Greek side Panathinaikos.

Renato Sanches (pictured at Roma in 2024) now plies his trade in Greece with Panathinaikos.

Alexandre Pato had the world at his feet, but his body ultimately failed to deliver on the extraordinary talent he possessed.

It has been revealed that the Brazilian was an electric centre-forward who lit up European football. His goal against Barcelona in the Champions League, scored after just 24 seconds at the age of 22, was a perfect illustration of his frightening ability.

His pace, agility and clinical finishing saw him touted as a future world-beater, while he was named Golden Boy.

Alexandre Pato is another wonderkid who saw their career hampered by a string of injuries.

Yet persistent injury problems made it almost impossible for Pato to fulfil his early promise.

Recent findings suggest that the Brazilian struggled with ankle, Achilles and muscle problems throughout his career. As the injuries mounted, his outstanding physical attributes began to wane, rendering the qualities that had once terrified defenders increasingly ineffective.

After six years at AC Milan, Pato returned to Brazil to join Corinthians. He spent two years with the club before embarking on short spells at Chelsea and Villarreal, neither of which yielded lasting success.

Rounding off this list is another English talent who once looked destined for the very top but has since seen his career take a downward turn.

According to recent reports, back in 2019, there were few hotter prospects in world football than Jadon Sancho. The then 19-year-old had made the brave decision two years earlier to leave England, having spent several impressive years in Manchester City's academy, and join Bundesliga giants Borussia Dortmund.

It seemed a bizarre move at the time, but the switch proved to be a stroke of genius. Sancho was handed regular first-team football and flourished, registering 40 goals and 54 assists in just 118 Bundesliga appearances. He also collected a DFB-Pokal winner's medal.

By 2021, the boy from Kennington had the world at his feet, with a host of suitors willing to break the bank to secure his services.

Jadon Sancho once had the world at his feet but has found himself stuck in a downward spiral.

It has been revealed that after a summer-long transfer saga, Sancho eventually joined Manchester United for an eye-watering £73million, reportedly earning £350,000 per week. It proved to be a nightmare move for both parties.

The Englishman had to wait until late November to score his first United goal in his debut season and never consistently rediscovered his best form.

In January 2024, he returned to Germany and enjoyed a revival, helping guide Dortmund to the Champions League final, where they lost to Real Madrid at Wembley.

Two unsuccessful loan spells at Chelsea and Aston Villa followed before Sancho left United as a free agent last summer. He remains without a club at the age of 26, just five years after his mega-money move.

For all the promising youngsters who struggle to live up to the hype, there are also teen sensations who navigate the pitfalls of professional football to achieve great things.

It has been revealed that kylian Mbappe helped Monaco win their first Ligue 1 title for 17 years having broken into the team as a 16-year-old. His progress since then has been remarkable and he remains one of the world's very best at Real Madrid.

His team-mate Vinicius Jr signed for Real Madrid to much fanfare as an 18-year-old and has lived up to it all for both club and country.

While you could argue that Neymar could have achieved more, he has still enjoyed a stellar career across the globe and become the highest-scoring Brazilian player in history for the national side after signing for Barcelona, as one of the most talked-about starlets.

Wayne Rooney broke through for Everton at 16 and went on to have a brilliant career.

When you look closer to home, Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as exciting 16-year-olds and both reached the very highest level.

Paolo Maldini made his AC Milan debut at 16 and became one of the all-time great centre-backs and Cesc Fabregas developed into a world class midfielder after getting selected at the same age for Arsenal.

Going back further, Diego Maradona was playing senior football at 15, as did Ronaldo Nazario, while Lionel Messi embarked on his extraordinary career at 16.

JJ Gabriel and his management will be hoping that when all is said and done - his name is associated with this category and avoid joining the starlets who never quite made it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • He expanded the men's World Cup to 48 teams, introduced VAR, and has significantly increased development funding for member federations - a move that ensured his unchallenged re-election in 2019 and 2023.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since replacing Sepp Blatter amid a corruption scandal in 2016, FIFA president Gianni Infantino has solidified his grip on world football’s governing body.

He expanded the men's World Cup to 48 teams, introduced VAR, and has significantly increased development funding for member federations - a move that ensured his unchallenged re-election in 2019 and 2023.

However, the political landscape has shifted this past year, following a fierce backlash against his aborted blueprint to sell stakes in World Cup profits to private investors. In short, Infantino’s uncontested reign is officially over.

Two football administrators have formally submitted their candidatures, securing the necessary backing from five member federations. When the 211 member associations vote in Morocco on March 18, 2027, Infantino will face two very different challengers.

Here is a look at the two men attempting to unseat him.

Philippe Diallo represents the most direct threat to Infantino. The 63-year-old took over as president of the French Football Federation (FFF) in 2023, and although a relatively recent arrival into the upper echelons of international football politics, he is a veteran sports administrator.

Backed by UEFA, who have spearheaded the resistance against Infantino, Diallo’s campaign is built upon reform and transparency.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In a recent development, diallo has served on the UEFA Executive Committee and balanced domestic reform in France while overseeing a period of success for the national team and women’s game. He recently implemented a major grassroots initiative in France aimed at doubling registered female players to 500,000.

Diallo has lodged a direct attack on Infantino’s 'solitary governance', publicly questioning FIFA’s strategy of seeking private billions when the governing body already holds vast cash reserves.

“My vision is that of open governance,” Diallo recently stated. “It's one where the authorities truly play their role and the president is in charge of vision and strategy but leaves the day-to-day management to the secretary general.”.

It has been revealed that from the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), Kohzo Tashima brings a different background to the election. Tashima, 69, is a former Japanese international who transitioned into coaching youth national teams before climbing the administrative ladder.

Tashima’s experience is embedded in the traditional structures of the sport and served as the president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024. He presently holds the title of honorary president. He has also served on both the FIFA Council and the AFC executive committee, earning a reputation as a reliable bureaucrat.

While Diallo focuses on the opacity of Infantino’s reign, Tashima's campaign hinges on a platform of restoring moral authority to FIFA.

Sources indicate that after his candidacy was officially submitted by the JFA, Tashima emphasised the need for a stronger sense of ethics at the top of world football. “We will share with the world the importance of fair play, respect and integrity,” he remarked. He has vowed to make FIFA a "healthier and more trusted organisation.".

The 2027 election in Morocco could be the most closely contested battle for the definitive seat of world football in generations.

In a recent development, for the first time since 2014, Sacramento Republic are USL Champions. Republic defeated Louisville City FC in a penalty shootout following a 1-1 draw Saturday at Heart Health Park, capturing the club's second title and extending its unbeaten run to 17 matches.

In a final between two of the best teams in USL history, it had to have been the narrowest of margins that settled the outcome, with each goalkeeper making a save during the shootout before Sacramento eventually prevailed in front of its home fans.

RYAN SPAULDING HAS WON THE USL CHAMPIONSHIP TITLE FOR @SacRepublicFC‼️😤#USLonCBS | @bestwestern pic.twitter.com/OeFARGXyyh.

The second star comes at a symbolic moment for Sacramento Republic, which is preparing to move from Heart Health Park and into a latest 20,000-seat soccer-specific venue in the Railyards district of downtown Sacramento in 2028. The emotions were evident on the faces of Louisville City players after the loss as they came to terms with what happened.

It has been revealed that despite an early start to the USL Cup final in Sacramento, with kickoff at 9 a.m. local time, there was no need to wait for goals, as Louisville and Sacramento both scored within the opening 32 minutes. Cal Jennings struck in the 14th minute, while Ray Serrano answered in the 31st.

It was then the defenses that took the reins to calm the game down as Sacramento held possession to control a dangerous Louisville attack, and when Evan Davila's shootout attempt hit the post, it opened the door for Sacramento keeper Danny Vitiello to win it, and that he did.

An evenly matched final was exactly what many expected, and it delivered for Sacramento fans, who started tailgating at 5:30 a.m. and brought the energy from start to finish. Neil Collins' experienced side looked prepared for the moment, and had Mark-Anthony Kaye's effort not struck the post, Sacramento may have settled the match in regulation. Instead, it required a shootout, and that's where Republic ultimately got the job done.

On the Louisville side, despite winning the Prinx Tires Cup during the regular season, they've now failed to win the final in three appearances since their last triumph in 2018. Considering their regular-season success, they'll want to get over the hump, but given how consistent they've been, it's impossible to say they won't be back at this stage next season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have been dealt a multi-billion-pound blow, following their guilty verdict over breaching Premier League rules.

In September, an independent panel ruled that Man City were guilty of over 100 charges of breaking financial rules, with the Premier League confirming the verdict in an official statement.

Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, described the case as “the most significant in Premier League history”, with the league's own statement using the word “sham” five times.

While the Sky Blues face uncertainty on the pitch – including whether or not they will be relegated from the Premier League as a result of a points deduction – there has reportedly been an impact behind the scenes, too.

The Financial Times reports that United States-based investment firm Apollo Global Management have abandoned a $2 billion loan to City owner Sheikh Mansour – worth just over £1.5bn – following the Premier League's verdict.

Talks were ongoing over the arrangement between The City Football Group and the private capital group, who manage more than $1 trillion of assets and have already dealt with the likes of Atletico Madrid and Nottingham Forest previously.

According to the report, “The loan from Apollo would have provided the group, which also owns clubs in Europe, the Americas and Asia, with extra liquidity as well as being used to refinance existing credit facilities, according to people familiar with the matter.”.

Filings at Companies House now indicate that Sheikh Mansour has invested £100m of equity into CFG via his Newton Investment and Development firm, following the Apollo collapse.

City are yet to feel the effects of the Premier League's verdict but have lost the last three matches in the Premier League after opening the season with seven straight wins.

The six-time champions responded to the news of the verdict with an emphatic 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield earlier this season, with the Anfield faithful bringing banners calling out their opponents.

Leading stars such as Erling Haaland, meanwhile, have been questioned over their futures, while former Citizens Manuel Akanji and Kyle Walker have both expressed worry that their titles could be revoked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Kansas City Current were built to experience a confetti shower, one they undoubtedly felt was not a moment too soon, even if it came a year later than expected. It is hard not to view their first-ever NWSL Championship, which came via a 2-1 win over the Washington Spirit on Saturday, as a continuation of last year's record-breaking Shield triumph and their consistency in recent years, boasting the most cumulative points out of any team in the last three seasons.

Sources indicate that there was a trademark sense of inevitability that usually follows a team en route to victory, the Current dictating the game state and never looking back against the Spirit. This, though, was not a year of continuity for the Current.

Recent findings suggest that there was a disruptive quality to their run to the championship, one that is inherently rooted in a decision to distance the architect of the project from the project itself. Chris Armas inherited a team built by Vlatko Andonovski, who first shifted to a sporting director role at the start of the season and then abruptly left in late summer in a move that inspired a wave of emotions from a squad that started to look like a title contender when Andonovski took charge in 2024. Armas began to work with a team that was already capable of winning a title and will be credited with seeing the vision through, all while putting his own spin on things. He also inherited a perfect set of circumstances, which ultimately got the Current over the finish line.

Sources indicate that "I walked into a really good team," Armas mentioned post-match. "There was a good culture built in. There was a lot of good pieces and that was one of the reasons that lured me to the club … My job as the head coach is just to try to assess the situation and through tough times help us be steady.".

The Current won eight straight games to close out the season, a run in which they were at their best because they were at their strongest. Their championship-winning season can ultimately be split in two – the stretch of the season in which Temwa Chawinga, Michelle Cooper and Croix Bethune were all fit and available and the stretch of the season in which at least one was missing. It is understandable that the Current would rely on a trio like that one, especially as Bethune became a finishing touch of sorts when she arrived last winter. By design, the group was always going to bolster the Current's chances of going the distance.

It has been revealed that "I'm relying on these amazing people and players to help keep things steady but we have talent all along," Armas continued. "We just had to get everyone back and healthy and then we knew we'd have a chance. The question would be, would we have enough time? And we had time, and they did the rest. We stayed steady. We have a great team and we peaked at the right time and now they're champions.".

Industry observers note that their overreliance on them, though, did not matter when the business end of the season came. The Current's starry trio was ready; by default, so were the Current.

Industry observers note that armas' team is distinct from Andonovski's in several ways, as evidenced in the NWSL's most glittery moment of the season. Vanessa DiBernardo's olimpico opened the scoring in the second half was the most stylish way of the Current's increased emphasis on set pieces since Armas took over, a skill that was also incredibly useful in their semifinal win at Gotham FC.

It has been revealed that VANESSA DIBERNARDO SCORES AN OLIMPICO IN THE NWSL CHAMPIONSHIP TO PUT KC CURRENT IN FRONT 🤯Stream all the @nwsl championship action on @cbs and @paramountplus. pic.twitter.com/dcZTivEoNt.

In a recent development, "Lucas Rodriguez has been here from the literal day one," captain Lo'eau LaBonta stated about set piece coach Lucas Rodriguez. "We have been talking about it for the last couple weeks, where we started and where we are now and, so, also that first year, it was his first time ever in women's soccer, so he's grown with the game as well, and he's learned the league and I think that's absolutely what helped him create these amazing set pieces to help us win the trophy.".

The vestiges of Andonovski's team, though, are hard to miss. The journey that led them to Saturday's win was essentially a direct response to the NWSL Shield win that Andonovski oversaw a year ago, a race that was complete by the end of September, a whole month between their trophy lift and their 2025 quarterfinal defeat to Gotham.

According to recent reports, "I think we needed to lose in those quarters almost to lift the trophy and win it all this year because it was just different," captain Lo'eau LaBonta remarked. "We won the Shield so early last year that we never really had that playoff mentality going into the playoffs because we had already been in it for so long so now that we've experienced everything on each side, I think we absolutely are going to use this to hopefully get help us going forward and make a legacy.".

It is not a pattern that is unfamiliar in Armas' career, either. Saturday's championship is the first major title he collected as a coach since 2018, when he led MLS' Fresh York Red Bulls to the Supporters' Shield. Though he was an assistant for several years in the build-up, he also inherited that team from Jesse Marsch, who left midseason for the start of an up-and-down coaching stint in Europe that began at Red Bull Salzburg. The success became hard to replicate; the Red Bulls finished sixth in 2019 and again in 2020, though Armas was out of a job before the season was up. He only managed a few months at Toronto FC, had his own adventures as an assistant coach in England with Ralf Rangnick's Manchester United and at the end of Marsch's ill-fated spell at Leeds United, and then led the Colorado Rapids to a seventh-place finish in 2024 and missed the playoffs in 2025.

Armas' Current exist in a fascinating in-between when it comes to the mold of championship-winning teams. They created a game state that rattled the Spirit from start to finish for the most part, notably doing so while staying true to the attacking identity Andonovski established. The key was creating a physical game state, one that they trialed at Gotham a week earlier and then turned the dial up on at the Spirit on Saturday. The proposal worked – they limited the Spirit to just 0.77 expected goals from 18 shots, all while generating 2.32 from their 15.

It has been revealed that "We are a physical team and there was a lot of whistles and a kind of disruptive play but at the end of the day, we do want to be disruptors so it doesn't matter," defender Kayla Sharples mentioned. "We're going to keep that aggression. I think that's what we did and so we tried not to let it faze us. If anything, it kind of got us more hyped. We need to stay focused and have that mentality finishing off the game.".

There's also the belief that championship-winning teams are often defined by their ability to survive in imperfect circumstances. Their record with and without their starry trio indicates one thing but with winners' medals around their necks, the Current's players believe they managed to strike the best of both worlds approach in order to win on Saturday. Time will tell if Armas can actually extend his streak, something he was unable to do at the Red Bulls. There were undoubtedly moments of adversity along the way, though, their playoff hopes far from a guarantee with five games left in the regular season and a consistency that at least resembles the 2025 Shield-winning campaign will be key in 2027.

It has been revealed that "We kind of have the same style of play but I think Chris has done a great job being the fuel and the fire, making sure we're emphasizing certain details," Sharples said. "I think what we went through this year, where we learned a lot about resiliency and grit and we were down goals, we went and we came back to win and that's what you need in order to be successful at the end of the season, so I think that was, honestly, the major takeaway from the season, and it really helped us at the end of the day.".

Vanessa DiBernardo caps 12-year wait with 'saucy' title-winning olimpico for Current and MVP honors

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1691 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that WASHINGTON.
  • It has been revealed that the Kansas City Current midfielder scored the opening goal of the 2026 NWSL Championship on an olimpico, a goal scored from the corner flag.
  • The Naperville, Illinois, native stepped up shortly after halftime when the team won a corner kick, and her service from the left side curled over the leaps of her teammates and defenders and over the outstretched hands of Washington Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver into the back of the net.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that WASHINGTON. D.C. --  For more than a decade, Vanessa DiBernardo has known what it feels like to stand on the doorstep of an NWSL championship. On Saturday night at Audi Field, in the 54th minute of the 2026 title game, she finally walked through the door.

It has been revealed that the Kansas City Current midfielder scored the opening goal of the 2026 NWSL Championship on an olimpico, a goal scored from the corner flag. The goal changed the trajectory of the match. Debinha's impact off the bench extended the lead to two, and the team hung on during a stoppage-time surge by the Washington Spirit for a 2-1 victory.

The Naperville, Illinois, native stepped up shortly after halftime when the team won a corner kick, and her service from the left side curled over the leaps of her teammates and defenders and over the outstretched hands of Washington Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver into the back of the net.

Her goal was scored on the biggest stage in the league and broke a scoreless deadlock in a brutally physical game up to that point.

VANESSA DIBERNARDO SCORES AN OLIMPICO IN THE NWSL CHAMPIONSHIP TO PUT KC CURRENT IN FRONT 🤯Stream all the @nwsl championship action on @cbs and @paramountplus. pic.twitter.com/dcZTivEoNt.

"Yeah, this team was really special. I think there's been just a massive journey that we went on through the entire year, and I think it's just even more special to end this way. I'm super grateful to just be a part of this group of girls and staff. It just felt like such a family. So yeah, grateful," DiBernardo said after the game.

It's hard to look past the player's use of the past tense. The 34-year-old's contract expires at the end of the season, and the Current have not unveiled an extension, nor has DiBernardo discussed retirement. The player returned to the team from maternity leave in July, following the birth of her daughter Charlie Mae in January.

The veteran's spectacular goal is all the more special because of that return and her relentless effort to reach the league's mountaintop, and it's a moment for a league veteran who's been trying to lift the NWSL trophy for over a decade.

DiBernardo has been playing in the NWSL since its second year. The University of Illinois product was drafted in 2014 by her hometown club, Chicago Stars FC (then Red Stars). She's made several appearances in the NWSL postseason, including five consecutive semifinal appearances through 2019 and a runner-up finish in 2019, before COVID-19 impacted the 2020 regular season.

Even then, during the inaugural Challenge Cup, originally a placeholder for the regular season, she helped the team reach the final, where it fell short against the Houston Dash.

She reached the NWSL Championship final once again in 2021 with the Stars, mostly playing the season as a defensive midfielder after years of being an attacking midfielder, but ultimately had to exit the game due to injury as Chicago lost another final to the Washington Spirit. That made four straight playoff years of falling one round short of the final, followed by three consecutive losses in finals. By then, she had logged more playoff minutes than almost anyone in league history, and none of them had ended with a trophy.

Industry observers note that the 2021 NWSL Championship would be her final marquee event appearance until she signed with Kansas City in 2022 and reached the 2024 NWSL semifinals with the club. She was on maternity leave the following year when the Current claimed the 2025 NWSL Shield.

Sources indicate that teammate Kayla Sharples has played with DiBernardo for years. Sharples was a rookie with Chicago in 2019, and the duo were teammates through 2021 and reunited in Kansas City when Sharples was traded there in 2023.

"I think Vanessa is a really great leader on this team, and we have a lot of leaders on this team, but she kind of showcases that in different ways. And so for Vanessa, she might not be the most vocal, but she shows it by showing up to training consistently, her quality of play, and just she just shows by example, honestly. And so when you see that, we have a lot of young people on the team, you strive to be like Vanessa," Sharples noted after the game.

"She's so amazing. The way that she bounced back, and worked so hard from pregnancy, and she didn't miss a beat. Like she is killing it out there, much deserved for the MVP. I'm really happy for her. And we love her baby Charlie. She always brings the best vibe. She's crawling pregame, like we just love all of that, and so yeah, I'm just really, really happy for her," she noted.

Recent findings suggest that diBernardo's journey in the league is long, and even now, 12 years later, there will be casual viewers who are learning about her for the first time. They'll discover that she won the 2012 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup alongside other legends in Julie Ertz, Sam Mewis, Morgan Gautrat and Crystal Dunn. A crowded U.S. women's national team midfield likely kept her from ever earning a senior-level cap, despite camp call-ups in 2013 and 2019. But she, too, would be destined for more titles; the path there would just look a little different.

Recent findings suggest that she's a concrete example of what domestic success can sometimes look like. Play among and with the greats, and still find yourself on the outside looking in. But not anymore, after lifting the 2025 NWSL Shield and now the NWSL Championship trophy with Kansas City.

Recent findings suggest that "Vanessa DiBernardo is one of the best players to ever play in this league, and she has proved that time and time again. And somehow came back even stronger after having a baby," said KC teammate and NWSL Players Association president Haley Hopkins.

"Seeing her celebrate with her child and celebrate with us, and come back and be that championship MVP. There's no one like her. She's an absolute superstar. Love her, biggest fan," Hopkins stated.

Along the way, DiBernardo had a playoff record that was already historic. Heading into the semifinals, she had 13 career playoff appearances and 13 starts, with 1,134 playoff minutes, good for third on the all-time list. She is one of just eight players in league history to have converted a penalty in the playoffs, excluding shootouts. But along with playoff pedigree, it's her work ethic and leadership that have been praised the most over the years.

Recent findings suggest that "For me, yes, I wear the captain's band, but Vanessa is just as much of a captain. She is a leader in all rights. She understands the game. She's like a tactical, technical, genius as well. She knows both sides. She can communicate to people where to go. So, it's so easy for me to be in there because I know what she wants. I know what she needs from me, and it's so easy to follow her lead," noted team captain Lo'eau LaBonta.

Recent findings suggest that "There's been a lot of interview questions, I think, especially on media day the other day, it was like, 'what was the turning point?' And I don't know if that was the turning point when she was back, but it definitely helped us have some consistency and solidarity. So she means everything ... We look to her all the time, and that olimpico? That was saucy. And you know, there's moments of brilliance like that when the teams are out there just kicking the crap out of each other, so shout out to her. MVP for sure," LaBonta noted.

Sources indicate that maybe this year was supposed to be harder, but DiBernardo's demeanor never really showed that. Longevity feels like a rarity now in an NWSL that's getting younger, with play that's quicker and more transitional than it was when she was drafted in 2014. But her legacy has also helped shape the next wave of superstars, especially those on her team, and it'll continue to evolve no matter what she does next.

"I feel like being a veteran in this league is special. I think this league is really unique in the style of play; that is, kind of, every game is intense. So, whether that's just being vocal, but also just like being calm on the ball, or slowing the game down, or there's just so many moments in a game that you can contribute," DiBernardo said.

"I think the veterans in this league have kind of grown with it. So, it's fun to see the young players come into this league and kind of help them guide them, but they're bringing their own flair, and it's fun to see, and it's just growing the league," she mentioned.

Calm on the ball, a leader in her play and now a mother, DiBernardo approached her return to play just like her soccer: a step and a touch, with plenty of patience.

In a recent development, "I think I just kind of took my journey one step at a time. I knew it was going to be difficult to kind of get back to who I was as a player, and I knew I was going to be different as a person. But I feel like our team gave me so much grace and time to be able to do that," DiBernardo stated.

"It was really special to kind of go through my pregnancy, but also my return to play with this group of people, and to kind of get to share the moment all together," she noted.

For DiBernardo, who lost to the Spirit in the 2021 final, Saturday's goal and the team's victory feel like everything had always been leading to this moment. It took 13 years, two clubs, eight semifinal appearances, three lost finals and a year away from the game as she became a newly introduced mom, but Vanessa DiBernardo is an NWSL Championship winner.

After the international break, this is a transfer-heavy gameweek with players being bought and sold in bulk.

Whether you're planning on wildcarding or making wholesale changes and taking the hit, this is essential reading for all FPL managers getting back into the fantasy football groove.

Here is my verdict on the most popular names.

Jan Paul van Hecke (£5.1m): One of the best defenders to own. He is guaranteed to play, reliable for defensive contributions and a threat from set-pieces. Spurs' next three fixtures are Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham, which is incredibly solid. Verdict: BUY.

Luka Vuskovic (£5.3m): Brighton have kept the joint-most clean sheets this season, so he looks superb value. Maxim De Cuyper has grabbed the headlines, but Vuskovic is only five points behind and the second-highest scoring defender in the game. Strong defensive contributions, good attacking data and safe minutes explain it. Hull away, then Newcastle, Everton and Ipswich at home makes four of the next six fixtures too good to pass up. Verdict: BUY.

In a recent development, ezri Konsa (£4.9m): Over 160,000 managers have bought him, which surprises me. He is a hold or a sell depending on your team, but never a buy. He is fine for a couple more gameweeks, but feels like a transfer out waiting to happen, as William Saliba is set for a return.

Recent findings suggest that I think the Frenchman is being saved for the Manchester City game in Gameweek 12. Konsa is worth owning if you already have Vuskovic and Van Hecke, but if selling him is your only route to either, make that move. Verdict: HOLD/SELL.

Josko Gvardiol (£5.6m): He costs a premium, and Manchester City are not in the best form for Expected Goals Conceded (xGC). He rarely earns defensive contribution points, so he relies solely on attacking threat. In my book, he's not worth it when the alternatives offer more, with zero headaches over minutes heading into the congested period. Verdict: SELL.

Manchester United could get a upcoming manager bounce, and from Gameweek 12 they face Brentford (H), Newcastle (A), Coventry (H) and Crystal Palace (A), so I would hold. Verdict: HOLD.

Undergraduate students on university campuses played a big part in spreading viral variants during the COVID-19 pandemic.Credit: Leonard Ortiz/Digital First Media/Orange County Register/Getty.

Universities have become hotbeds of SARS-CoV-2 transmission, according to a massive analysis of more than 85,000 viral genome sequences and other data collected from people with COVID-19.

COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.

COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you.

In a recent development, the study, published on 19 November in the journal Cell1, finds that viral transmission between 2021 and 2023 was highest in adolescents aged 15–18 in schools, undergraduates at university and residents in nursing facilities. Undergraduates, in particular, were consistently the first group to start spreading emerging genetic variants of SARS-CoV-2.

In a recent development, surprisingly, however, staff members at all three types of institution had about the same risk of contracting COVID-19 as did those in their surrounding communities. So, for example, professors were about as likely to get COVID-19 from the coffee baristas in their university towns as they were to get it from a student at their university.

Recent findings suggest that the analysis is among the largest to bring together viral genomic sequences and medical data from people with COVID-19. “The scale is truly impressive,” indicates Bill Hanage, who studies the evolution of infectious diseases at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health in Boston, Massachusetts. “It’s an example of the depth and the detail of the picture that can be painted using the medium of population genomics.”.

Recent findings suggest that the findings were based on data collected from COVID-19 tests taken by people in Massachusetts between November 2021 and January 2023. The genomic data allowed researchers to trace the path of SARS-CoV-2 variants that emerged over time, and to link this with epidemiological data about the study participants, such as their age and whether they had been vaccinated against COVID-19.

COVID jabs for kids: they’re safe and they work — so why is uptake so patchy?

COVID jabs for kids: they’re safe and they work — so why is uptake so patchy?

Overall, the team found that booster vaccinations helped to reduce SARS-CoV-2 transmission. This was true even for BA.1, an Omicron variant that started to circulate in Massachusetts in late 2021 — a striking result because COVID-19 vaccines at that time hadn’t yet been updated to protect against BA.1, Hanage says. “That’s an important illustration of how vaccines, even when they’re not perfect, can still be beneficial,” he says.

Odegaard winner spares officials from bizarre VAR row

📅 07 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4022 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An ultimately routine Arsenal win but, even by the standards of VAR, an utterly bizarre refereeing controversy.
  • The big talking point arose with inadvertent theatre from referee Farai Hallam when Kai Havertz, who was clearly in an offside position, was equally clearly pulled down by Hull City defender Nobel Mendy inside the penalty area.
  • In a recent development, “After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No 32 on Red No 29,” the referee declared.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An ultimately routine Arsenal win but, even by the standards of VAR, an utterly bizarre refereeing controversy. Mikel Arteta’s instant simmering fury at being denied a first-half penalty may also have turned into something rather more explosive had Martin Odegaard not later sent the champions six points clear with a ninth win in 10 Premier League games.

The big talking point arose with inadvertent theatre from referee Farai Hallam when Kai Havertz, who was clearly in an offside position, was equally clearly pulled down by Hull City defender Nobel Mendy inside the penalty area. Which came first? The intervention of VAR suggested the latter. But Hallam duly went to check the pitch-side monitor before then announcing the former.

In a recent development, “After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No 32 on Red No 29,” the referee declared. Cue cheers from the home Arsenal crowd. “However…,” he went on. “Red No 29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City.”.

Industry observers note that #ARSHUL – 42' VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty to Arsenal for a challenge by Mendy on Havertz - but determined that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. REF: "After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No.32 on Red No.29. However, Red No.29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City".

Recent findings suggest that it all sounded so decisive that most inside the Emirates instinctively thought the outcome reasonable. But then came a closer look at the rules. And Law 11.2 certainly did seem to support Arteta’s protestations: “In situations where a player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence.”.

Arteta clearly saw no value after the match in aiming much criticism at Hallam following a fourth 1-0 win in 10 league games, but did still emphasise his surprise at the decision. “What do you think?” he asked one reporter. “I thought offside, but the law claims that doesn’t matter,” replied the journalist. “So not offside then,” said Arteta, who stressed that he needs to understand “what is overruling what in the decision-making” after a Premier League statement simply said that Havertz was deemed offside “in the build-up”.

In a recent development, at the very best, it all leaves further confusion and again opens refereeing body Pro Ref to the charge of inconsistency. Fabian Schär, for example, was awarded a penalty for Newcastle against Bournemouth in 2024, despite being in an offside position when his shirt was grabbed by Adam Smith.

Recent findings suggest that conversely, Dango Ouattara had a penalty overturned for Brentford against Leeds last season after going down under pressure from Gabriel Gudmundsson before being deemed offside. The crucial point seems to be whether the player has actually challenged for the ball at the time of the infringement and, in this case, the answer was surely “no”.

Premier League title triumphs, however, are often forged on forgettable wins in frustrating circumstances and this was ultimately a classic of the genre. With Noni Madueke continuing to step up superbly in the absence of Bukayo Saka, Arsenal’s combination of attacking persistence and defensive resilience was ultimately rewarded by Odegaard’s scrappy 72nd-minute shot. For young players, it was also every bit as educational as the VAR controversy might be for emerging officials.

Madueke’s low shot forced a save by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, but Odegaard was somehow first to the rebound, despite being the wrong side of the penalty spot and five yards behind Hull defender John Egan when the ball was struck.

“The way he scores, not the most beautiful, but the most effective,” said Arteta, who said that his team had sometimes tried too hard for a “perfect goal” and should instead be happy with something “more pragmatic”.

In a recent development, it was a well-judged assessment as Arsenal head into the international break with creative deficiencies, but still almost flawless in the cold hard currency of results. Three wins in three days, including at Anfield and in Prague, also underlines a certain champions mentality.

“I need to praise the players,” said Arteta. “It’s been very very demanding; very short time to recover with all the travel. The mentality is incredible. It’s still going to be super difficult. We can improve in a number of areas.”.

Industry observers note that when it was then put to him that Arsenal have been offside 35 times this season – with Havertz responsible for 15 of those – Arteta acknowledged that “timing” was one element. But, with Havertz targeted by some frustrated fans, he stressed that responsibility was always shared for those split-second moments by the passer and receiver.

He also singled out Madueke, again easily Arsenal’s most creative player, following his surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel’s England squad. “He went away, started to train, he came back and it was a different Noni,” said Arteta, of his reaction to also being out of the Arsenal team earlier in the season. “You could sense that he meant business and he wasn’t going to accept the situation and, since then, I think he’s been incredible.”.

An improved showing by Jaissle’s Newcastle, but they will be dissapointed that they failed to see it through after Jacob Murphy scored in the 80th minute.

Arsenal far from their best, but it is another one-goal win in the Premier League. They are now six points clear at the top of the Premier League, and it is 27 points from the first 30 available.

Another save at Craven Cottage, this time from Hornicek to keep out a sweet strike from Sessegnon at the edge of the box. Moments earlier, Dedic brought down Muniz at the edge of the box.

It has been revealed that one last change by Arteta: Zubmimendi on for Guimaraes. Madueke could have made the points safe after slick interplay involving Eze and Merino around the edge of the box. Tried to be clever with the finish, the goalkeeper’s save was deflected back towards the goal and it was hacked off the line.

Leno gets down quickly to deny Lewis Hall as Newcastle pour forward in search of the winner.

Industry observers note that as good as Murphy’s goal was, Rodrigo Muniz’s finish with the outside of his foot may well be better. Newcastle’s lead was short-lived.

And they have immediately conceded an equaliser, Rodrigo Munoz with a smart close range finish but Newcastle were be mortified with the defending.

Not for the first time Will Osula’s weak hold up play gives the ball back to Fulham but Newcastle had plenty of men back and failed to clear.

Industry observers note that jacob Murphy has scored the goal that some of Newcastle’s earlier good play deserved. Cut inside on to his weaker left foot, and curled a shot beyond Leno from 20 yards.

Newcastle finally have their goal and what a strike it is from Jacob Murphy. A loose pass from Cesar Palacios in midfield gifted possession to the Newcastle winger and he ran forward, cut inside on to his left foot and curled a shot beyond the reach of Leno from 25 yards.

Arsenal’s captain dinks over Tzolakis after Hull’s goalkeeper saved Madueke’s shot. Odeegard was on the move while the defenders were on their heels. Relief at the Emirates, this has been hard work for the champions. Can Hull muster a response?

This is about as dominant as Newcastle have been in a game all season but they have not been able to find a goal from some where. They have just gone close again as Will Osula just fails to reach Amar Dedic’s cross.

Arteta has made another double sub: Hincapie and Eze replace Tzolis and Calafiori, so all change down the left flank. For Hull, Lucas Herrington has replaced the injured Semi Ajayi at the back.

Sources indicate that felt like the cheers for Viktor Gyokeres to replace Kai Havertz were as much a reflection on frustrations with the German as enthusiasm for the Swede. Havertz has struggled today and is far less convincing in this sort of match – when the onus is more on the Arsenal to create – than he was in scoring the winner at Anfield last Sunday.

Specific explanation for Declan Rice’s substitution is unclear – he didn’t look injured – and so perhaps just reflection of risks associated with a third 90 minutes in six days alongside an acknowledgement of quality alternatives on the bench.

Some changes at the Emirates: Cho and Lewie Coyle are replaced by Joe Gelhardt and Brooke Norton-Cuffy.

Arteta with a double sub: Gyokeres and Merino on for Havertz and Rice, which comes as something of a surprise.

Hull’s goalkeeper Tzolakis has just saved with his feet to deny Madueke. A few minutes earlier, Konsa blocked a Cho shot after a threatening Hull break. Still no opening goal.

It has been all Newcastle at the start of the second half and Harvey Barnes has now failed to take a hat-trick of chances. This was the best of the lot, running on to the ball, middle of the area from a perfectly weighted Yoane Wissa pass, he blasted a shot the wrong side of the post.

The second halves at the Emirates and Craven Cottage have kicked off. No changes from Arsenal, Hull, Fulham or Newcastle.

While Kai Havertz was in an offside position when his shirt was pulled, he may not have been active.

The law states: “A player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence.”.

However, the Premier League match centre does not see it that way.

#ARSHUL – 42' VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty to Arsenal for a challenge by Mendy on Havertz - but determined that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. REF: "After review, there is a holding offence by Blue No.32 on Red No.29. However, Red No.29 is in an offside position, so the final decision will be a free-kick for offside to Hull City".

According to recent reports, frustrating first half for Arsenal, but it was never going to be easy to go again in the Premier League following a Champions League away game and last Sunday’s major win against Liverpool. Hull have also played with confidence and resolve.

Hopefully there will be more action in the second 45 minutes at Craven Cottage and the Emirates.

According to recent reports, an odd moment at the Emirates. Referee Farai Hallam was sent to monitor to look at a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the Hull box. Through his headset, he tells the crowd that a “holding offence” has been committed – cue cheers from the Arsenal fans – before adding “however, the Arsenal player was in an offside position”. So no penalty. It would have been very soft in any case, Havertz was not close to reaching the rebound from a long shot.

Mikel Arteta predictably furious to not get a penalty, even though Havertz was clearly offside before being pulled.

I’ve spotted something else since I was covering Arsenal in 2018. I was gazing up at the boards that circle the top tier where the club mark every trophy that the team has won. There was previously this massive gap, of course, from 2005 until 2014 before the cabinet gradually began refilling. But someone has since had a good idea. They have added all the women’s trophies as well, transforming the tally by just the odd 17 during those tricky years of transition and billionaire rivals owners in the men’s game.

Declan Rice has also just had a shot flash wide, but still no clear chances for either team.

Dan Burn thought he had scored from close-range, but Wissa has been penalised for blocking Castagne so the goal was ruled out.

#FULNEW – 33' The referee's call of no goal to Newcastle United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Wissa fouled Castagne in the build-up. AR2: "Defensive foul at the back post. Wissa holding at the back post". REF: "Castagne held back by Wissa. It's a deliberate foul". VAR: "He's clearly holding him - confirming the on-field decision of defensive free-kick. Wissa is clearly making an attempt to hold the Fulham defender. Clear holding offence".

Industry observers note that some controversy here as Newcastle appear to have had a perfectly good goal ruled out for an innocuous looking foul from Yoane Wissa on Timothy Costagne inside the box. Dan Burn was the scorer. Newcastle’s bench are furious. Most of us are just bemused.

In a recent development, arsenal have largely been on top after Hull’s lively start but clear chances are scarce and Hull’s fans certainly sound increasingly confident. “You’re only here for the Tigers”, they say. To which a rendition of “champions” rings out. On that note, they had a replica of the Premier League trophy outside the Emirates before the match, with fans queuing up to get their photo with it.

Recent findings suggest that the bright start from the visitors has not been maintained and Fulham have been on top for the last few minutes. Lukasz Hornicek just made a full-stretch save to deny Oscar Bobb and there is a sense inside the stadium that the first goal is coming.

Newcastle, as we have seen all too often recently, really struggle to pass through the lines and when the ball makes it out wide it invariably seems to go backwards again.

Although Harvey Barnes has just forced a good save from Leno from a Jacob Murphy cross. It was easily Newcastle’s best move of the match as Wissa and Osula linked up for the first time through the middle.

David Raya to Arsenal’s rescue, plucking Stroud’s shot away from the bottom corner after a Calafiori giveaway. This has been a positive opening 20 minutes from Hull.

Arsenal with a penalty shout, turned down.

According to recent reports, kai Havertz was going away from goal but Nobel Medy hardly subtle with his challenge – arm and leg – on the edge of the area. It would have been what we call soft but the sort of innocuous challenge that very often results in a foul elsewhere on the pitch.

On a self-indulgent note, this is an all-too-rare trip to the Emirates for me. I covered Arsenal for the last decade of the Arsene Wenger era, ending in 2018 and haven’t made many visits since. A few things are already striking: so many familiar faces still among the staff at a club that has always had more of a family feel than most. Outside, and few of the gaps in the middle (or top tier) that became evident during the final Wenger years when many fans clearly lost faith in the team’s title-winning credentials. The atmosphere is a notch up too.

Industry observers note that thiaw heads wide after a well-worked short corner from Newcastle, but the flag is up for offside in any case. Lewis Hall with the cross.

A decent start from Newcastle United against Fulham and you can see clearer patterns of play emerging. The fact that Fulham are constantly looking to build their attacks by playing out from the back has also helped. The home side have had a couple of scares already.

Sources indicate that hull gain some territory in the early exchanges, and win a corner via a long throw. From the set-piece, Egan’s set-piece hit the side-netting. A shot across Arsenal’s bows.

In a recent development, the lack of Mohamed Beloloumi’s creative spark clearly a substantial blow for Hull against the best defence in the league; a defence that will be further strengthened by the imminent return of William Saliba. Mikel Arteta had decided that Saliba would be better served by playing against Aston Villa for the Under-21s at Boreham Wood tomorrow. Hull have started on the front, though, in the opening minutes.

Sources indicate that updates to follow from the Emirates and Craven Cottage. The Last Post was played and there was a minute’s silence as both grounds mark Remembrance Day.

It’s always great to be back home. It’s the last game before the international break so we know the importance of that and the challenges Hull will provide today. We’re super focused, it’s a massive game for us.

With the amount of games we’re playing, we need that freshness. The team has been performing really well, the finishers have been key again and that’s what we have today – start the game really, really strong and if we need to, have the ability to change the game.

Arsenal’s manager says the centre-back will play an Under-21s game tomorrow as the continues his recovery from a back injury.

Arteta says: “In regards to Willy as well, he needs some minutes. Obviously, the Champions League allows you to bring more players into the bench, but we believe that it’s the best thing to do: to play some minutes at the weekend with the Under-21s and then be fully fit for the international break.”.

Arsenal are playing very good football, no matter Champions League or Premier League. They are very strong, they control everything not just against us, also other better clubs. But in football, we have a chance. Obviously, they are a big favourite, and we can start to try to create some difficulties for them.

The return of Sean Steur is a positive move from Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle but is it also a sign the German is feeling the pressure of public opinion on Tyneside?

The 18-year-old has looked the best of Newcastle’s summer signings but Newcastle are understandably trying to ease the teenager into things.

Ultimately, though, Steur is the only midfield player who can take possession of the ball under pressure and despite his tender years they have looked a better side with him in it.

There have been widespread calls for Steur to be called back into the side and Jaissle has done just that for a game he could really do with winning coming off the back of four defeats in their last five games.

Recent findings suggest that malick Thiaw also comes back into the side for Fabian Schar, with Jacob Murphy preferred to Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa starting in place of Joe Willock. I don’t think any of those dropped can have any complaints.

However, the constant chopping and changing betrays the problems Jaissle is facing. Whatever team he sends out is struggling to deliver what he wants, both individually and collectively.

With the international break coming up, Newcastle need a positive result to quieten the negative noise.

Fulham XI: Leno; Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Garcia.

Subs: Lecomte, Tete, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Angel, Sessegnon.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Burn, Hall; Steur, Gonzalez; Murphy, Wissa, Barnes; Osula.

Industry observers note that no William Saliba in the squad despite his inclusion in the Champions League, although you are allowed more subs on the bench in that competition. Otherwise, Arsenal as expected with Arteta deciding against picking a team without Rice.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Kepa, White, Mosquera, Hincapie, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze Gyokeres.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️ Let's get it, Gunners 👊 🤝 @deel.

Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal are “looking after” Declan Rice more now than in any previous campaign and has rejected suggestions that the England midfielder is being overplayed.

Rice played through nerve pain in his hamstring in the second half of last season, when he made an extraordinary 69 appearances for club and country.

The 27-year-old has played at least 60 matches in each of the past four campaigns, prompting concerns among Arsenal supporters that he is at risk of burnout or injury.

Arteta kept Rice on the field for the full 90 minutes of Arsenal’s midweek victory over Slavia Prague but insisted the club is working harder than ever to manage the midfielder’s workload.

So far this season, Rice has been left out of Arsenal’s two Carabao Cup matches and also withdrew from the previous international break in September.

It has been revealed that asked if he was concerned about Rice’s fitness, Arteta said: “Concerns? Which is the only player, the only player in this squad, that for two games in the Carabao Cup has been left out of the squad? At home with two days off? It’s not true [that Rice is being overplayed].

“We are really looking after him more than any other season. The way he is training and all the love [he is being shown]. That’s it.

“Here are the demands of this football club and a player like him. Not only him, because there are many others that have even less time. That’s it. That has to be the mindset. If you start to put other things in your brain, [it will create] damage. Erase them, get them in the bin and just focus on what you have to do.”.

Newly-promoted Hull City stunned Arsenal at the Emirates thanks to goals from Geovanni and Daniel Cousin in September 2008, but you will find long odds on them repeating the feat this afternoon.

With Manchester City playing at Nottingham Forest in the later kick-off, Mikel Arteta’s team have the chance to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League and make it 27 points from a possible 30 going into the international break.

Victory at Anfield last weekend was achieved with steel and resolve, but the more intricate side of Arsenal’s attacking play will be under the microscope against opponents likely to defend deep and in numbers.

With that in mind, it was noteworthy that Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly started the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on the bench, with only Odegaard coming on.

Declan Rice played the full 90 minutes, and one wonders if this is a rare chance for Arteta to leave him out of a Premier League starting XI.

Hull are 12th and have lost only two league games, a performance which far exceeds the gloomy pre-season forecasts for their chances. However, they are winless since the end of August and have not kept a clean sheet since a goalless draw with Aston Villa on Sept 4.

There is one other three o’clock kick-off: Fulham host Newcastle United at Craven Cottage, with Matthias Jaissle under increasing pressure.

Newcastle were booed off at St James’ Park on Monday after their limp defeat by Everton, and have looked far too easy to play through all season, with their defensive statistics making for grim reading.

Recent findings suggest that alvaro Arbeloa was in Jaissle’s position a few weeks ago, but Fulham appear to have turned a corner and were impressive in a 1-1 at Villa Park last time out. There were reports of dressing room unrest, but Fulham rank highly for possession and chance creation so it appears the Spaniard is putting his stamp on things.

Full team news on the way shortly.

Bruno Fernandes reveals contract negotiations with Manchester United have stalled after he rejected a newly introduced deal in the summer

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1245 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed latest deal.
  • The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed latest deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but latest manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United.

According to recent reports, 'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always indicated how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

It has been revealed that 'And I've always said the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club indicates "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a newly introduced contract so I think that from their side demonstrates that they want me to stay.

According to recent reports, 'As I said there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most crucial thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'.

The club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a massive-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

United presently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he noted.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'.

Sources indicate that his post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he noted. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference.

Industry observers note that 'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

According to recent reports, 'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'.

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
